identification.summary: Blue Tsunami is Microsoft's tracking name for Black Cube, which Microsoft's CYBERWARCON 2023 post calls a well-known mercenary actor (private-sector offensive actor, PSOA) [S1]. LinkedIn's Threat Prevention and Defense team presented how Black Cube used honeypot profiles, fake jobs and fake companies on LinkedIn for reconnaissance and human intelligence (HUMINT) operations against targets with access to organizations of interest to its clients [S1]. This is a social-engineering and HUMINT actor, not a malware developer; no exploited CVEs or malware are cited in the sources gathered.
identification.firstObserved: LinkedIn said the Hungary operation began in 2020 [S2]. Meta removed Black Cube-linked accounts in December 2021 [S4]. Microsoft/LinkedIn public disclosure of the Blue Tsunami name: 2023-11-09 [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Blue Tsunami (Israel, private sector offensive actor) [S7]. Black Cube is the underlying private intelligence firm; Reuters describes it as based in Israel [S2]. Black Cube denies hacking and says it works on litigation and white-collar crime within legal advice [S2][S4]. Do not merge with other Microsoft Tsunami-named PSOAs (for example Caramel Tsunami/SOURGUM, a spyware vendor); they are separate clusters.

attribution.sponsor: Commercial: a private intelligence firm acting for paying clients; no state sponsor is stated in the sources [S1][S2]. LinkedIn did not say who the Hungary operation worked for [S2].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft equates Blue Tsunami with Black Cube in its own post [S1]. Attribution of the Hungary operation to Black Cube is LinkedIn's statement as reported by Reuters [S2]. Black Cube disputes the characterization [S2][S4].
attribution.basis: LinkedIn Threat Prevention and Defense investigations presented at CYBERWARCON 2023 [S1][S2]; Meta's December 2021 account takedown as reported by press [S4].

objectives: Client-driven reconnaissance and human intelligence: obtaining access to and information from individuals with access to organizations of interest to Black Cube's clients [S1]. In Hungary, recorded video conversations were used in a campaign to discredit NGOs [S2]. Meta described its personas as seeking targets' personal email addresses, likely for later phishing [S4].

sectors: Human rights and NGO workers (Meta-described persona themes) [S4]
targeting.notes: LinkedIn said at least 12 activists and journalists critical of Prime Minister Orban were targeted and recordings were published in pro-government media before the April 2022 election [S2]. Meta said the firms collectively targeted about 50,000 people across its platforms (all the surveillance-for-hire firms in the takedown combined, not Black Cube alone) [S4]. Customers described by Meta ranged from private individuals to law firms and companies [S4].

capabilities.summary: Network of fake personas posing as employers or recruiters with bogus job listings and fake company pages to contact targets on LinkedIn, then moving to off-platform video conversations that were recorded [S1][S2]. Meta described personas posing as graduate students, NGO workers and film or TV producers to obtain personal email addresses [S4]. Black Cube says it does not phish or hack [S4]. No malware, exploits or CVEs are attributed in the sources gathered.

campaigns.name: Hungary NGO and journalist targeting
campaigns.summary: Per LinkedIn via Reuters, fake personas with bogus job postings contacted at least 12 activists and journalists; off-platform video clips were later used to discredit NGOs ahead of the April 2022 election. LinkedIn removed the accounts and company page.

campaigns.name: Meta takedown of Black Cube network
campaigns.summary: Meta removed about 300 Facebook and Instagram accounts tied to Black Cube using fictitious personas; Black Cube said it does not operate in the cyber world.

campaigns.name: Microsoft and LinkedIn disclosure at CYBERWARCON 2023
campaigns.summary: Microsoft publishes the Blue Tsunami name for Black Cube and summarizes LinkedIn's presentation on honeypot profiles, fake jobs and fake companies.

diamond.adversary: Black Cube, tracked by Microsoft as Blue Tsunami; commercial private intelligence firm reported as Israel-based [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Fake personas, fake job postings and fake companies for HUMINT and elicitation; recorded video calls [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Social platform accounts and company pages on LinkedIn and Meta platforms, plus off-platform video calls [S2][S4]. No technical infrastructure indicators in the sources.
diamond.victim: Activists, journalists and NGO personnel in Hungary; broader individuals with access to organizations of interest [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Commercial intelligence for hire, with outputs used in a political discrediting campaign in Hungary; the client was not named [S2].
diamond.technology: Reliance on professional social networking and open recruiting channels, with weak identity verification of employers and recruiters [S1][S2].

gaps: Clients and tasking are not identified; LinkedIn did not say who the Hungary operation served [S2].
Microsoft's primary text was seen only via a short fetched excerpt of the 2023-11-09 blog; the LinkedIn slides themselves were not obtained [S1].

Reuters and OCCRP/Meta coverage were read only as search-result summaries; direct fetches failed. Meta's original December 2021 report was not opened, and account counts differ across outlets [S2][S4].
Malpedia and MISP entries were seen only as search summaries and are community catalogs, not primary sources [S6].
Black Cube denies cyber activity; no technical (malware, infrastructure) evidence is public in the gathered sources.
Activity after 2023 and any additional Microsoft or LinkedIn reporting were not found.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the human and social layer: professional networking and messaging platforms where personnel are recruited, and personal email accounts [S1][S4]. STEP 2: Actor is a commercial HUMINT provider using fake employers and personas; it relies on trust and careers, not exploits [S1][S2]. STEP 3: Template is fake recruiter or job post, then off-platform video call, then recording or personal email harvest [S2][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued elicitation and discrediting-oriented collection against NGOs, journalists and activists for paying clients. MDCOA, speculative, is use of the same pretexting against cleared or defense-adjacent personnel for a client interested in them; no source shows this. Candidate indicators: unsolicited recruiter contact from new profiles or thin company pages, pushes to move to off-platform video calls, and requests for personal email addresses [S2][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: fold PSOA social-engineering reporting from platform providers into insider-threat and counterintelligence awareness, not only network defense. (2) Authorities: this is not a network intrusion, so reporting runs through counterintelligence and security channels rather than only cyber incident reporting [S1]. (3) Mission assurance: personal accounts and off-duty channels are the exposed surface; personnel awareness is the main control [S4]. (4) Coordination: coordinate with platform trust-and-safety teams such as LinkedIn and Meta, which produced the only public detection [S1][S2][S4].
